function_question: How does a computer learn from examples?

opening.text: There was a helpful robot called Pixel who got a new job in the school kitchen.
Pixel tried to sort the fruit, but it just guessed at random and got almost everything wrong.
Pixel thought: "Nobody can write a rule for every fruit. What if I could LEARN from examples instead?"

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: Chaos in the kitchen
chapters.line: Pixel mixes up almost every fruit. This time, nobody writes the rules.

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Pixel asks for help
chapters.line: How would you teach a friend who has never seen an orange? Pixel needs a teammate.

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: Learning is everywhere
chapters.line: You and Pixel spot machine learning all around you.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of features
chapters.line: The clues share one secret: learn from examples, not rules.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: The feature-card lab
chapters.line: No magic, just a checklist! Pixel hands you 10 fruit pictures.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The feature map
chapters.line: Every feature that tells two things apart gets a branch.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The data plan
chapters.line: Great training starts with a plan for varied pictures.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The new-picture test
chapters.line: Train, test on 10 new pictures, add variety, and test again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: Pixel can see
chapters.line: Pixel sorts the kitchen fruit correctly, even fruit it has never seen.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Pixel keeps mixing up the fruit, and it needs to learn from examples. Can you help Pixel get above 80% correct on pictures it has never seen? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some trainers already have a plan for teaching. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Machine learning is everywhere. Tap each card to meet four real-world learners!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four learners share…
guide.skill: Unplugged first! Which feature card sorts the most fruit right? Predict, then score 10 pictures. In the Machine Trainer, use photos of objects only, never faces.
guide.sketch: Time to plan your data like a real AI trainer!
guide.build_and_test: Train the Machine Trainer, then test it on the 10 pictures you set aside. How many does it get right?
guide.retry_tip: Add more VARIED examples, retrain, and test again on the same 10 pictures!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Pixel sorts the school kitchen's fruit like a pro, because YOU taught it with great examples!

quick_check.question: Pixel gets 7 out of 10 new pictures right. What is its accuracy?
quick_check.right: Right! 7 ÷ 10 = 70%. Pixel needs 9 out of 10 to get above the 80% goal.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Correct ÷ total: 7 out of 10 is like 70 out of 100.

predict.prompt: Good plan or bad plan for training Pixel? Predict first!

items.label: 20 oranges in different light and angles

predict.explain: Varied examples teach the features that really matter. And testing on training pictures is like marking your own homework, so always test on new pictures!

lab.title: The feature-card lab
lab.predict: Which feature card will sort the most of your 10 fruit pictures correctly?

tool.name: Mind map
tool.intro: A mind map grows ideas like a tree, from one big idea in the middle. Today you'll use all 5 pieces to find the features that tell your two classes apart.

parts.name: Centre
parts.what: Put the big question in the middle.
parts.example: 🚲 In the middle: How can I make my bike safer?
parts.starter: In my centre I'll write my two classes: oranges vs…

parts.name: Branches
parts.what: Draw the main topics coming out.
parts.starter: My four branches are colour, shape, texture and…

parts.name: Twigs
parts.what: Add smaller ideas to each branch.
parts.example: 🚲 On "lights": front lamp, back reflector, flashing mode.
parts.starter: On my texture branch, the twigs are…

parts.name: Pictures
parts.example: 🚲 A tiny bell doodle next to "noise".
parts.starter: A quick doodle for "bumpy skin" could be…

parts.name: Links
parts.what: Join ideas on different branches with a line.
parts.example: 🚲 Link "reflector" to "helmet": both help drivers see you.
parts.starter: The features a camera can actually see are…

sketch_checklist: I chose my two classes and aimed for 20 training pictures of each.
I planned different lighting, angles, sizes and backgrounds.
I set aside 10 new pictures for testing.

test.check_question: Find one picture the machine got wrong. Which feature fooled it?

reflection.question: AI check: your classifier learned from your pictures. Would it still work on someone else's photos?
options: ✅ Yes, if my examples were varied
🤔 Maybe, if their light is similar
❌ Not if their photos look very different
